pr_title: Feature: Redesigned the left hand sidebar
pr_body:
This PR migrates the SideBar implemenation away from the NavigationView control to our own written control, making feature development and styling a lot easier.

Fixes #12930

ToDos:
- [x] ~Update minimal pane to cover entire side (if desired)?~
- [x] Animate expanding/collapsing pane
- [x] Animate expanding/collapsing items
- [x] Update styling of sidebar to match design
- [x] Keyboard handling
- [x] Proper drag and drop handling
- [x] Fix initial state being wrong
- [x] Fix cursor when hovering over the Grid Splitter
- [x] Add back double click (on the Grid Splitter) to collapse/expand the sidebar
- [x] Fix issue where right clicking item triggers a click
- [x] Add tooltips (big tooltips for drives are another issue)
- [x] Reordering favourites might crash and reset favourites
- [x] Double clicking resizer leaves it in weird visual state
- [x] Restore pane width between sessions
- [x] Restore compact mode between sessions
- [x] Fix icon in the network section
- [x] Fix the tooltip for OneDrive


**Screenshots (optional)**
![Animation showing the different behaviors for the new sidebar](https://github.com/files-community/Files/assets/16122379/8fd95f66-01f5-4438-ac2a-d79c31843636)

## The problem

I've managed to find the race condition that was causing the icons not to load (or rarely load) on the sidebar when plugging a USB drive. The race condition happens between `SideBarItem.UpdateIcon()` and `DriveItem.LoadThumbnailAsync()`.

When a USB is plugged in, the `UpdateIcon` method is called first which grabs the `IconSource` from its `Item` property:
![image](https://github.com/files-community/Files/assets/53011783/a83ef7c7-d3bf-4244-9f85-a82e76ac52e1)

Peeking into the `DriveItem.IconSource` property, the `Icon` used to set the source is null - this is because the method to load the icon (`DriveItem.LoadThumbnailAsync()`) did not complete before updating the icon:
![image](https://github.com/files-community/Files/assets/53011783/ee022a4c-875c-43d7-8efe-5fc286e7efa9)

After more investigation, I've discovered that setting the `Icon` property will also call `PropertyChanged` for the "IconSource". That event is supposed to be handled in the `SideBarItem.ItemPropertyChangedHandler()` method which calls the `UpdateIcon()`. This would in turn negate the effects of the race condition:
![image](https://github.com/files-community/Files/assets/53011783/f3d3c2c1-ef33-4367-858a-d7d2fbfe634a)
![image](https://github.com/files-community/Files/assets/53011783/ece5874d-c21d-4138-9138-4715965b2edf)

The event itself is not hooked properly and the method to do so (`SideBarItem.HookupItenChangeListener()`) is never called **after the sidebar item is added**.

(Also, `HookupItenChangeListener` contains a typo 💀)

## The solution
The easiest fix would be to call `HookupItenChangeListener()` when a new item is added.
The harder way would be to refactor the code behind 🤷‍♂️

@d2dyno1 Thank you for your help in debugging this but I'm afraid this is not the issue. When running the app with the latest commit (where the typo is also fixed), the handler does work properly. 

The issue is that the Drives have their icon loaded twice with varying results. You can run the app and add a breakpoint in the "LoadThumbnailAsync" method of the drive item. I was able to see it hit twice for every drive (easiest to debug when adding a USB drive). The interesting part is that the IconData seem to change between runs of that method which is probably the culprit here.

The race condition is still there. Putting a breakpoint below `Icon ??= await IconData.ToBitmapAsync()` will trigger only after the icon is updated in SideBarItem and with no subsequent calls to the `UpdateIcon()` method.

`UpdateIcon()` method tries to grab the value from `IconSource` which itself uses the `Icon` property, and since it's called before `LoadThumbnailAsync()` can complete - the `Icon` to use as the source is null.

To prove my theory, I've changed the `IconSource` property to use an icon that's never null:

issue_context.title: Feature: Display sidebar options when right clicking headers
issue_context.body:
### What feature or improvement do you think would benefit Files?

Hi,

I was recently struggling to show the libraries section on the sidebar. I tried to show options by clicking the parent menu items like "Drive", "Home" to get the options menu, because I couldn't find it anywhere in the settings. Then I was told that I need to right click on a small blank space to change the menu items options. I think that's a bad UX and many people wouldn't find this on their own.

I clicked where the red dot is:

10.0.22631.1972
